rules.multipliers: 29 Sep 2026: all three audiences' tiers are low/middle/high price points inside the evidenced willingness-to-pay range (Peacock p.177; Business/_working/revealed-wtp-quote-history-2026-09-29.md). The middle is a price buyers have actually paid or agreed. The x1.4 / x1.75 multipliers no longer apply to consultancy; software editions keep them.
rules.public_policy: Craig 29 Sep 2026 (D5): no consultancy prices on any public surface. The only public figure is Clarity Check £600. No tier tables, no audience menus, no software figures, no add-on prices, no implementation figures, no day rate or day counts on any public surface. Full figures live in the audience price sheets sent after a raised hand (DO-SOP-015).
rules.software_presentation: Every software price is shown two ways in proposals/packs: buy outright, or finance lease at the rate card. Never monthly alone.
rules.day_rate: Internal only. Never publish 720 or any multiple (1440, 2880, 5760, 360, 1080) as a price.
rules.upgrades: Moving up any ladder (Works, Proof, Commerce; Proof -> Works Connected; Proof+CRM+Floor -> Works Scaled) costs only the outright price difference (or that difference on finance) plus any extra implementation/labour. Nothing already paid is lost. Craig 25 Sep 2026.
rules.finance_presentation: Client documents show software outright plus ONE monthly figure over 36 months (3 years). 48/60 kept for reference only. All prices indicative; fixed at the audit. Craig 25 Sep 2026.
rules.standard_features: Accounts connection (Xero/QuickBooks/Sage) and open API + webhooks are standard in every Works edition (Proof: API in all, accounts from Proof+CRM). Value absorbed, no base lift. Trade/B2B portal belongs to Decoded Commerce, not Works. Extras are named and POA. Craig 25 Sep 2026.
rules.rounding: Craig 28 Sep 2026: every level is Essential x1, x1.4, then x1.75 on that, rounded to clean steps: under £1,000 to nearest £50; £1,000–£10,000 to nearest £100; above £10,000 to nearest £500; software monthlies to nearest £10.
rules.segmentation: Craig 29 Sep 2026: place every prospect by scope profile (sites, systems, entities, staff, who signs), not turnover. Turnover is a cross-check. £500k-£1m firms land in Owner-led or Managed team by scope. Tag WTP interview notes with the audience.
rules.presentation: Craig 29 Sep 2026 (revised): present tiers the way Peacock does (Pricing for Success pp.186-193). Each tier shows its price AND its cumulative feature list, so the list visibly grows from Essential to Complete (the 'feature ladder' diagonal). Items a tier adds are highlighted; response-time items replace the lower tier's rather than repeat. Middle tier labelled 'Recommended'. For proposals, use Peacock's consultancy format: options listed down the page with descriptions that lengthen as the price rises. Group cards add 'Multi-company programmes: quoted.' No programme figure.
rules.indicative: Craig 29 Sep 2026: every sheet and card is an indicative guide, sent after the segment is qualified. Same deliverables in every segment; a smaller segment costs less because the work takes less time.
rules.tiers_vs_segments: Craig 29 Sep 2026: tiers differ by what's delivered (tier_summary, full list in DO_Service_Value_Matrix); segments differ only by price (the work takes less time for a smaller business). Response times, on-site frequency and board output belong to the TIER, never the segment. Segment scope shows only audit coverage (sites/systems).

owner_led.label: Owner-led
owner_led.profile: One site; owner runs operations; 2-3 systems at most; under ~15 staff; owner decides alone
owner_led.buys_against: off-the-shelf software (DecoNetwork, Shopify), doing it themselves, doing nothing
owner_led.metric: fixed price per project; monthly only after an audit

managed_team.label: Managed team
managed_team.profile: One or two sites; a manager layer; 3+ systems that need joining up; 15-50 staff
managed_team.buys_against: hiring an operations manager (about £123k over two years), an agency, a local developer

scope.audit: up to 2 sites, full systems estate

group.label: Group
group.profile: Several sites, entities or brands, or 50+ staff; board or finance director signs
group.buys_against: in-house IT team, the ERP vendor's services arm, a large consultancy

scope.audit: all sites and entities, group consolidation
scope.deliver_service: same-day response, on site every 6-8 weeks

tier_summary.essential: Written findings and the fix order, every problem sized in £. One visit, 30-min walkthrough.
tier_summary.recommended: Adds the buy / build / leave-alone call on every system, integration map, supplier-feed check, and a firm price for the fix. 60-min walkthrough.
tier_summary.complete: Adds a second on-site visit and a board-ready summary for a funder or co-director. 90-min walkthrough.

recommended_adds: Buy / build / leave-alone call on every system

tier_summary.essential: One workstream from the plan, delivered monthly. Remote, 3-day response.
tier_summary.recommended: Adds parallel workstreams, vendor management, process documentation, quarterly on-site and review. 1-day response.
tier_summary.complete: Adds concurrent workstreams at hard-deadline pace, on site every 6–8 weeks. Same-day response.

availability.owner_led: existing clients only (after Deliver), priced at the Deliver level; never offered cold

tier_summary.essential: One transformation stream, milestone-planned, monthly written progress. 3-day response.
tier_summary.recommended: Adds systems, process and people moved together, vendor selection, team training, quarterly leadership review. 1-day response.
tier_summary.complete: Adds concurrent streams, data and reporting build-out, a handover so it doesn’t depend on me, board attendance. Same-day response.

recommended_adds: Team training as changes go live
complete_adds: Handover so it doesn’t depend on me

availability.owner_led: existing clients only (after Deliver), priced at the Deliver level; never offered cold

tier_summary.essential: Named contact, direct line, monthly sessions and deliverables. 3-day response.
tier_summary.recommended: Adds vendor management, process documentation, quarterly on-site and review. 1-day response.
tier_summary.complete: Adds data and reporting build-out, team training and handover, board attendance. Same-day response.

small_business.ruling: Craig 19 Sep 2026 (qmu821g9o03): Clarity Check survives as the sole fixed-price small-business product. AI Readiness Check and Quarterly Sprint retired. Small-business Deliver/Transform/Retained ladders retired; sub-£1m buyers use the S1 figures above. 28 Sep 2026: Clarity Check £600 (rounded), offered to both under-£1m segments (S1 and S2); small businesses now have their own segment (S1, under £500k) with every service priced for it. 29 Sep 2026: Clarity Check £600 offered to Owner-led only; it is the single public price.
